summary: Baltimore County tower at 9405 Old Harford Road, managed by the Forest Service; the structure stands with its cab gone and the platform is used for research; no build date found.

facts.status_note: The tower structure stands, but the cab is no longer in place, according to the Forest Fire Lookout Association.

access.note: The survey's DNR land unit is the Baltimore County Project Office, Cub Hill Ranger Station; a 2002 student page says residents could not go up the tower.

visit.trail_note: The survey gives the access point on the left side of Old Harford Road, north of Summit Avenue.

events.note: Deed dated 24 July 1942 for the site; the survey gives the tower installation date as unknown

notes_for_editor: No build date in any source I read; the survey gives the installation date as unknown. A search snippet attributed a 1943 date, a 120 ft height and a Western Union antenna to a DNR poster (and a 1983 replacement line, ambiguous as to which tower it refers to). I could not open the poster (HTTP 404), so none of that is used; the survey table's 125 ft conflicts with the snippet's 120 ft. The date the cab was removed is unknown. The survey does not say the ranger station is Forest Service property, so the story gives only the DNR land unit it names. The survey calls the platform by that name and does not say the top of the tower is a platform, so the story does not say so. The UMBC page is from summer 2002, so its statement that climbing cannot happen is dated. A search snippet suggests Barbara Garner's 2012 book A View from the Top covers individual towers; not checked. The easternuslookouts.weebly.com Cub Hill page has a title only and no text. Height is not converted to metres because the survey does not say where it is measured.
